variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables don't need to be declared. $0 is the whole line, $1, $2 are fields.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Awk implicitly converts between strings and numbers depending on context.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Standard C-like operators. String concatenation is done by placing strings adjacently (e.g. "a" "b").

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Pattern-action structure itself acts as a conditional, or use explicit if-else in blocks.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Standard C-style for loops. Useful for iterating over fields in a line (NF = Number of Fields).

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Custom functions can be defined. Local variables should be added as extra parameters.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: Arrays in Awk are actually associative arrays. split() creates a 1-indexed array.

maps.title: Associative Arrays
maps.notes: All arrays are associative (maps). Very common for counting occurrences.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Awk relies on checking return values of functions like getline or system().

comments.title: Comments & Script Headers
comments.notes: AWK uses # for comments with script headers.

numbers.title: Numbers & Arithmetic
numbers.notes: AWK supports shell integer arithmetic and numeric expressions.

booleans.title: Booleans & Exit Codes
booleans.notes: AWK evaluates boolean status through exit codes (0 = success) and boolean primitives.

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Coercion
type_casting.code:
str_val="42"
# Arithmetic context forces integer coercion
num=$((str_val + 0))
type_casting.notes: AWK handles type conversion explicitly via type accelerators [type] or arithmetic evaluation.

strings.title: Strings & Quoting
strings.code:
single='Literal single quotes'
double="Expanded: ${USER}"
multiline="Line 1
Line 2"
strings.notes: AWK differentiates between single quotes (literal) and double quotes (variable expansion).

string_formatting.title: String Interpolation
string_formatting.notes: AWK provides in-string variable interpolation and printf formatting.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Case
pattern_matching.notes: AWK matches patterns with case statements or switch blocks with glob matching.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.code:
# Brace expansion
for i in {1..10..2}; do
    echo "$i"
done
range.notes: AWK constructs ranges with brace expansion {start..end} or range operators ..

iterators.title: Pipes & Iterators
iterators.code:
while IFS= read -r line; do
    echo "$line"
done < "file.txt"
iterators.notes: AWK streams data elements through command pipelines and loop iteration.

oop_classes.title: Classes / Structured Functions
oop_classes.notes: AWK defines reusable components through classes (PowerShell 5+) or modular functions.

lists.title: Arrays & Collections
lists.code:
items=("apple" "banana" "cherry")
items+=("date")
echo "${items[0]}" # apple
echo "${items[@]}" # all elements
lists.notes: AWK manages arrays using array lists @() or whitespace-delimited shell arrays.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: AWK emulates tuples through string delimiters, .NET Tuples, or positional variables.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Lists
sets.notes: AWK models unique sets using associative arrays or underlying runtime sets.

modules_import.title: Sourcing & Modules
modules_import.code:
# Source an external script
source ./utils.sh
# or: . ./utils.sh
modules_import.notes: AWK imports external functions using source (. in POSIX) or Import-Module.
